mechanism_narrative: A rising FEDFUNDS rate above 4% in the current month predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to increased near-term discounting of equity expectations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS > 4.0, or FEDFUNDS decline follows and reverses the prediction.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in PAYEMS (labor market activity) by at least 2% month-over-month precedes a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as hiring momentum boosts corporate optimism.
failure_condition: No significant positive return (t-test p > 0.05) over 60 days after the labor activity threshold is crossed, or the effect persists only in contractionary regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both HOUST (industrial production) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 1% in the same month predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return through stronger aggregate demand.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically significant (p > 0.05) when both proxies rise together, or the effect is absent in contractionary conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of at least 3% over three months predicts negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns as weak manufacturing signals investor pessimism.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive or indistinguishable from baseline (p > 0.05) during the INDPRO decline, or the effect is not robust across multiple cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4% triggers a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as lower labor market friction lowers discount rates and boosts equity valuations.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive (p > 0.05) when UNRATE crosses below 4%, or the effect reverses when rates rise again.

mechanism_narrative: When PAYEMS falls by more than 5% in a month, the S&P 500 exhibits negative 60-day forward returns as weak labor demand signals corporate caution and reduced investment.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the PAYEMS decline, or the effect is absent in non-recessionary contractions.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent inflation spike as measured by CPIAUCSL exceeding 225 for two consecutive months predicts negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns due to expectations of tighter policy.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative (p > 0.05) during the inflation spike, or the effect is absent outside the U.S. inflation shock context.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in GDPC1 (GDP) and HOUST (production) by at least 2% in the same quarter predict a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as stronger aggregate demand supports equity valuation expansion.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when both proxies rise together, or the interaction is not statistically significant.
